thesis: The apparent cardiovascular benefit of moderate drinking (the 'J-curve') is largely an artefact of confounding and abstainer (sick-quitter) bias; once addressed with Mendelian-randomization and pooled individual-participant analyses, there is no cardioprotective threshold and total harm rises roughly monotonically with intake, so there is no risk-free level of alcohol.

positions.name: Classic J-curve cardioprotection
positions.gist: Pooled prospective cohorts show light-to-moderate drinking (about 1-2 drinks/day) is associated with roughly 25% lower coronary and cardiovascular mortality versus non-drinkers, tracing a J/U-shaped dose-response.

positions.name: HDL biological-plausibility mechanism
positions.gist: Interventional data show alcohol raises HDL-cholesterol and apolipoprotein A-I and lowers fibrinogen, a mechanism predicted to cut CHD risk by about a quarter, lending the J-curve causal biological plausibility.

positions.name: Abstainer / sick-quitter bias
positions.gist: The apparent protection largely disappears once ex-drinkers who quit for ill health ('sick quitters') are no longer misclassified into the abstainer reference group and study-quality artefacts are controlled.

positions.name: Mendelian randomization: no causal cardioprotection
positions.gist: Using genetic variants that lower alcohol exposure (ADH1B rs1229984 in Europeans; ALDH2/ADH1B in East Asians) as unconfounded instruments, less alcohol predicts better cardiovascular profiles and lower CHD/stroke, refuting a causal protective threshold.

positions.name: Pooled IPD and GBD: no risk-free level
positions.gist: Large individual-participant pooled analyses and the Global Burden of Disease find the lowest-risk level of total consumption sits at or near zero, with all-cause and most cardiovascular harm rising roughly monotonically with intake.

positions.name: Residual low-dose benefit / all-cause-vs-CVD distinction
positions.gist: Even in rigorous pooled and MR analyses, myocardial infarction/ischaemic heart disease retains a modest inverse association with light drinking, so a small genuine cardioprotective signal may persist though it is outweighed by stroke, cancer and injury harms.

positions.name: Pattern / beverage-not-dose (French paradox)
positions.gist: The cardiovascular association is attributed to drinking pattern (regular moderate frequency) and wine's antiplatelet effects rather than total ethanol dose, implying a simple dose-response 'no safe level' framing is misspecified.

benchmark_claims.claim: Light-to-moderate drinking vs non-drinkers, CVD mortality and CHD incidence
benchmark_claims.value: CVD mortality RR 0.75 (0.70-0.80); CHD incidence RR 0.71 (0.66-0.77); lowest risk at 2.5-14.9 g/day

benchmark_claims.claim: Effect of 30 g/day alcohol on HDL and predicted CHD risk reduction
benchmark_claims.value: HDL +3.99 mg/dL; predicted 24.7% CHD risk reduction, ~68% mediated by HDL

benchmark_claims.claim: All-cause mortality RR for low-volume drinkers after adjusting for abstainer bias
benchmark_claims.value: Adjusted RR 0.97 (0.88-1.07), not significant, vs 0.86 unadjusted; 87 studies

benchmark_claims.claim: Low-volume drinkers vs lifetime nondrinkers, all-cause mortality (2023 update)
benchmark_claims.value: RR 0.93 (0.85-1.01, P=0.07); increased risk from 25 g/day (women), 45 g/day (men); 107 studies

benchmark_claims.claim: Mendelian randomization: ADH1B A-allele and coronary heart disease
benchmark_claims.value: CHD odds ratio 0.90 (0.84-0.96); systolic BP -0.88 mmHg; 261,991 participants

benchmark_claims.claim: Genotype-predicted alcohol (per 280 g/week) and stroke vs MI (China Kadoorie)
benchmark_claims.value: Ischaemic stroke RR 1.27 (1.13-1.43); MI 0.96 (0.78-1.18, NS); 512,715 adults

benchmark_claims.claim: Minimum-risk threshold and CVD-subtype gradients per 100 g/week (83-study IPD)
benchmark_claims.value: Lowest all-cause mortality ~100 g/week; stroke HR 1.14; MI 0.94; 599,912 drinkers

benchmark_claims.claim: Level of alcohol minimizing total health loss (GBD 2016)
benchmark_claims.value: Zero drinks/day ('no safe level'); ~2.8 million alcohol-attributable deaths globally in 2016

benchmark_claims.claim: Drinking frequency (pattern) vs quantity and MI in men
benchmark_claims.value: MI RR 0.63 (0.54-0.74) at 5-7 days/week vs <1/week; frequency mattered more than beverage type
